test_cases.prompt: ground-the-claim on resources/2026-08-08-design-tokens.md, a freshly clipped source with no literature note yet
test_cases.expected_output: Reads the whole source, identifies the source's Core Idea and a right-sized list of candidate claims (merging any that share the same underlying reasoning before presenting them), surfaces both (e.g. 'this source's core idea seems to be X. It's talking about: A, B, C — which do you want grounded, or is there something I missed, or something that should be combined or split differently?'), lets the user pick a subset, add their own, or reshape the list, then runs one independent /grounding call per selected claim, writing each confirmed claim to the literature note incrementally as it's confirmed — declarative heading plus condensed Evidence, not batched at the end. Ends with a batch pass finding terms/entities the claims lean on.

test_cases.prompt: ground-the-claim on resources/2026-08-08-design-tokens.md, where the literature note already has one confirmed claim from a prior session
test_cases.expected_output: Reads the existing literature note's ### claim headings first, and only offers candidates not already covered — does not re-surface the already-grounded claim, and does not re-write the Core Idea line.

test_cases.prompt: ground-the-claim on a candidate whose derived filename already exists on disk with unrelated content
test_cases.expected_output: Stops and asks the user to reword the claim or confirm a genuine duplicate, rather than auto-disambiguating the filename.
